name: LAKESHORE OPEN: Great Lakes Unaugmented Marathon
description: The LAKESHORE OPEN is a 200-kilometer unaugmented endurance race tracing a course along the reclaimed Great Lakes shoreline through Meridian 88's outer corridors, passing through Tier 2 industrial districts, Shelf borderlands, and the contested green corridors of the lakeshore reclamation zones. The race is one of the few sporting events that physically passes through multiple tiers, requiring competitors to navigate both the environment and the social architecture of the city. Verification is rigorous; the governing council, the Lakeshore Athletic Compact, operates independently and is funded entirely by entry fees and community sponsorship.
story_hooks: A veteran LAKESHORE OPEN runner discovers that the course through the Shelf borderlands this year passes directly over a site where something was buried — and someone does not want the race to happen.

A Tier 1 competitor who has run the race eleven times without finishing is this year's quiet favorite — and has attracted the attention of a corporate recruiter who wants to understand how she trains.

The Lakeshore Athletic Compact receives a large anonymous donation contingent on a minor course modification that would route the race away from a specific Shelf district for the first time in the event's history.
